clue.text: French King's personal capital

parts.note: Hugh Capet was a medieval King of France, founder of the Capetian line
something personal is one's own

explanation.surface: A remark about a French monarch who has a capital city of his own.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('has'), not a possessive belonging to the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The South African city is one of that country's seats of government, its legislative capital.

clue.text: Severely criticize the clothing

explanation.surface: A reviewer savages the costumes.
explanation.definitionFit: To slam hard or beat is one sense; British slang also uses it for gear or garments.

clue.text: Work to keep the wolf from the door

definitions.text: Work to keep the wolf from the door

parts.words: Work to keep the wolf from the door
parts.note: a book or piece written purely to earn money and stave off hunger, not for art

explanation.surface: Toil done to stave off poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' looks like labour; it is a literary work, written to keep the cooking pot full.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack novel produced only to pay the bills.

clue.text: Article about South Africa's saint

parts.note: the is the definite article
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A piece of writing on a South African holy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('is'), not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Teresa of Avila is a celebrated holy woman of the Catholic Church.

clue.text: Breaking the law, an alien writer

indicators.note: Breaking means the word law is broken up and its letters reshuffled

parts.note: a Pole is a foreigner from Poland, an alien to a Briton

explanation.surface: A foreign author who flouts the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: Horace Walpole and Hugh Walpole were both English novelists.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace Walpole wrote the Gothic novel The Castle of Otranto.

clue.text: Craftily lead diamonds after ending in three no-trumps

indicators.note: after places the diamonds piece behind the earlier letters
ending in a word points to the final letter of the word three

parts.note: NT is the bridge abbreviation for no-trumps
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Bridge talk: a player cunningly leads a diamond at the end of a three no-trumps contract.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge setting makes 'lead' look like a card play; together with 'Craftily' it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure someone by cunning persuasion is to tempt them.

clue.text: End halfway through exam — in test, time's up

indicators.note: halfway through means only the first half of the word exam is used
in places the turned time inside the test word

parts.note: to try is to test

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word time is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: time, with 's as a link

explanation.surface: An invigilator calls time halfway through an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses the word for time, and 'in' puts that reversal inside the word for test; 'halfway through' keeps only the first half of 'exam'.
explanation.definitionFit: The furthest point or limit of something.

clue.text: Discolour, like a pool?

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake or pool
the suffix -ish means like or somewhat

explanation.surface: Asks whether something stains in the way a pond does.
explanation.walkthrough: A TARN is a small mountain lake in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To dull or stain the surface of metal.

clue.text: Grant at one time put in three consecutive letters …

indicators.note: put in tells us the time phrase goes inside the run of letters

parts.note: C, D and E follow one another in the alphabet
once means formerly or at one time

explanation.surface: A permission given long ago, linked to the next clue by the dots.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join this clue to 12 down in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow or admit something is to yield it.

clue.text: Operating during race, doctor is vigilant

parts.note: a machine that is operating is on

indicators.note: during here means the doctor sits within the race

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
a healer is one who doctors the sick

explanation.surface: A medic who operates mid-race must keep a watchful eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is the famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man; 'during' sets the doctor inside it, and the whole clue reads as one scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Being watchful and ready for danger is an idiom for keeping a lookout.

clue.text: Called by name in a newspaper

indicators.note: in signals the name abbreviation going inside the newspaper word

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone is named in print in the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Called is the past tense of telephoned, as in rang a friend.

clue.text: Stony bed, where it took a different course

definitions.text: bed, where it took a different course

explanation.surface: A rocky river bed at the place where the stream changed direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stony' is short for stony broke, penniless; the second reading is cryptic: a river bed where the water burst out over the wide plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Stony broke and the phrase both mean utterly penniless; a river that burst its banks and spread out took a new course.

clue.text: Round meadows bird is free

indicators.note: Round tells us the bird wraps around the meadows

parts.note: a ree is a female ruff, a wading bird
leas are meadows or pastures

explanation.surface: A bird circling the fields is at liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like an adjective for the meadows but tells the bird to go round them.
explanation.definitionFit: To set loose or liberate is to let go.

clue.text: … full three notes, post-like

parts.note: full is slang for drunk, as is stoned
E, A and F are notes of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Continuing 7 down: letters spelling out a tune, flat as a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post-like' comes from the phrase 'as deaf as a post'.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely unable to hear, like a post.

clue.text: Tense, having drunk a small measure

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
an en is a small printing measure, half an em

explanation.surface: Someone nervous who has knocked back a modest tot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like a verb with 'having', but is the adjective; 'having' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To tense muscles is to make them taut.

clue.text: Spectre — he creates a feeling of horror

indicators.note: creates means the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A ghost that brings on fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creates' looks like the verb of the sentence; it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a sense of fear or revulsion.

clue.text: Endlessly show off bull, perhaps Irish bull

indicators.note: Endlessly means the last letter of the show-off word is lopped

parts.note: to parade is to show off
an ox is a bovine animal

explanation.surface: A boastful bull, possibly an Irish one.
explanation.walkthrough: An Irish bull is a self-contradictory statement, such as 'I was a fine baby but they changed me'.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-contradictory statement is a kind of absurdity of logic, of which the Irish bull is one example.

clue.text: A game cut down

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A match curtailed.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a text is to condense it.

clue.text: It alleviates mental distress when wrongly annoyed

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters are set out incorrectly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A soothing remedy for someone who is unfairly irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkiller or soothing thing that relieves suffering.

clue.text: Tree hailing from Mediterranean island

indicators.note: hailing suggests a word called out, so the island name is heard spoken

parts.note: Cyprus is an island in the eastern Mediterranean

explanation.surface: A tree that originates on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hailing from' reads as 'coming from', but is the signal that the island's name is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: The cypress is a tall evergreen conifer.

clue.text: Picture of convict imprisoned by old king

indicators.note: imprisoned by puts the convict word inside the king

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry monarch of the nursery rhyme
a lag is a convict, an old lag

explanation.surface: A portrait of a prisoner locked up by an ancient monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An artwork of pasted-together pieces.

clue.text: Tool incorporated in a second

indicators.note: in places the company abbreviation inside the word for a

parts.note: per means a, as in once a week

explanation.surface: An implement built in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' here means 'per', as in 'ten pounds a head'; 'in' sets the company abbreviation inside it, and the surface hides that 'Tool' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripping implement with jaws.

clue.text: Used a test to reveal drugs

indicators.note: to reveal tells us the answer is uncovered inside the words used a test

explanation.surface: A test was used to show up narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drugs' looks like a noun; it is the verb, as in calms with a tranquilliser.
explanation.definitionFit: To calm with tranquillisers.

clue.text: I handled orders for boiling fowl

indicators.note: boiling suggests the letters seething and churning into new places

explanation.surface: A kitchen worker took orders for a chicken to be boiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boiling fowl' looks like a phrase of its own; 'boiling' is the anagram signal and 'fowl' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a breed of domestic chicken originating in an American state.

clue.text: The starting date some say is about 4th of July

annotationWithheld.why: The starting date some say is about 4th of July (1-3): D-DAY; 'The starting date' defines it, but no parse of 'some say is about 4th of July' giving D-DAY has been found.
annotationWithheld.clue: The starting date some say is about 4th of July

clue.text: Hire workers and start to take action

parts.note: to engage staff is to hire them
men are workers, as in management and men

indicators.note: start to points to the opening letter of the word take

explanation.surface: Take on staff and begin to do something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' looks like the object of 'take', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A military battle is called an engagement.

clue.text: Concerning this, the lady's adversary comes round

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman

indicators.note: comes round means the adversary word turns about and is read backwards

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

explanation.surface: On this point, the woman's enemy eventually relents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes round' reads as being persuaded; it is the signal that the enemy word turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal legal adverb meaning of or about this document.

clue.text: Keeps its press in order

indicators.note: putting the letters in order means arranging them afresh

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their printing press tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' looks like tidiness; it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on doggedly is to continue, as one keeps going.
